title: Abba, son of the executed Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Yevamot 15a tells that Abba married the daughter of his brother Rabban Gamliel and had another wife. Abba died childless. His wife, his brother’s daughter, was an aylonit, so his brother Rabban Gamliel performed levirate marriage with her co-wife.

notes.text: The consulted story appears in Yevamot 15a, not the printed 46a. It confirms the brother, niece, co-wife and aylonit relationships. The mismatched source locator is retained as a question.

Supplied Yevamot46a stays beside the inherited15a comparison; no new whole primary passage or manuscript was inspected. The final אחיו explicitly repeats his brother and is restored in the English. RabbanGamliel is written fully earlier in the supplied narrative. The story’s niece, brother and co-wife relationships are translated as Hyman presents them, not admitted into an authority genealogy; aylonit is not ordinary childlessness.

The photographed Hyman notice (vol. I, p. 55) reads Yevamot 15a. The supplied Hebrew transcription gives 46a. Yevamot 15a names Abba as Gamliel’s brother and says that Gamliel himself performed levirate marriage with his daughter’s co-wife. The discussion offers several accounts of why the co-wife was permitted. Hyman’s heading supplies the paternal identification separately.
